what: grant-remove: the CLI revocation path that the card's honest-limits list named as missing ('kein Grant-Entfernen (Handedit)'), measured with a test-first ladder and a mutation battery
hypothesis: A scope can only be taken away by hand-editing a security-relevant JSON file. The product refuses hand edits everywhere else (grant_file_* refusals, atomic writes, seal provenance), so a revocation path built on the loader + atomic rename should be reachable and should take effect on a LIVE daemon's next request without a restart.

defect.evidence: git grep -c 'grant-remove' on tree bf72775 = 0 in bin/, README documents only grant-add and seal-grants; the card's limits list says 'kein Grant-Entfernen (Handedit)'. `signerd grant-remove` on bf72775 exits 1 with an unknown-command refusal (measured as T1-T5 all RED).
defect.class: 4th recurrence of the linear-reader/surface class on this card (grant-create README dead-end, keystore_exists, grant-add 2nd-scope, now removal)

rulesKept: the product's own loader (src/grantfile.js loadGrantFile) is the judge: directory mode/owner, kernel read lease, file owner+mode, schema, every remaining grant, seal when a passphrase is given
atomic temp(O_EXCL,0600)+fsync+rename; inode changes so a pre-opened write descriptor is orphaned
survivors copied through from the loader's parsed grants, not re-serialized by this code
symlink refused (grant_file_symlink), same defect measured on grant-add 2026-11-05
a sealed file is re-sealed as part of the act; a sealed file without a passphrase is refused (grant_file_sealed) so a rewrite can never destroy the seal
a passphrase given for an unsealed file is refused (grant_file_unsealed) - --seal-passphrase-file must never mean 'seal now'
unknown name changes NOTHING and the refusal names the grants that are in the file (grant_not_found + in-file list)
limits: removal is BY NAME: it removes the whole scope, it does not narrow a cap
a grant removed while a request is in flight is judged by the loader read at the START of that request
a wrong passphrase refuses (the seal is never destroyed unauthenticated)
no freshness/lock check: two concurrent grant-remove processes are not serialized beyond the loader's read lease
no audit log of who revoked what - the file carries no author

ladder.note: all 12 are RED on the pre-fix tree, including the guards: the instrument IS the fix (there is no removal command to guard). This is stated rather than papered over - no test here is a false-positive guard on the pre-fix tree.

mutationBattery.how: each mutation applied to the working tree, `node --test test/grant-remove-surface.test.js`, then byte-restored (src/grantadd.js + bin/signerd.js + README.md)

caught.mutation: the removal loop no longer skips the named grant (removal removes nothing)
write in place (copyFileSync) instead of temp+rename - not atomic, inode preserved
drop the grant_file_sealed refusal - a sealed file is rewritten without a passphrase
drop the symlink refusal - follow the link
swallow the grant_not_found refusal text in the CLI
remove BOTH README occurrences of grant-remove
rewrite the survivor's CONTENT (expiresAt forced to a new value)
reverse the survivor's key order (bytes change, parsed content equal)
caught.result: RED 11/1 AFTER G6 was strengthened; 12/0 before it

caught.mutation: a sealed file is removed but never re-sealed

firstBatterySurvivors.mutation: removed ONE of two README occurrences
firstBatterySurvivors.whySurvived: bad mutation, not a weak test: the other occurrence still matched the T4 regex; the corrected mutation (M6b, both occurrences) is caught
equivalent mutant - the round trip is byte-identical for these values (measured: json.dumps equality holds)
equivalent mutant - src/grantfile.js contains no skipMode option, so the mutation changes nothing (grep -c skipMode src/grantfile.js = 0)

realGapFound.statement: G6 was named 'byte-identical' but asserted deepStrictEqual on the PARSED grant only, so a key-order rewrite (M7c) passed while the file bytes changed
realGapFound.fix: G6 now compares JSON.stringify of the survivor (byte-level serialization) BEFORE the content comparison
realGapFound.retest: M7c -> 11 pass / 1 fail (G6 RED), working tree -> 12/12

liveVerification.t2: a daemon started with two grants signs a payroll tx (exit 0), grant-remove runs with NO restart and NO signal, the SAME daemon then refuses that grant with grant_not_found on its next request, and the surviving grant still signs (exit 0)
liveVerification.inode: T1 asserts the grant file's inode CHANGES across the removal (rename, not truncate-in-place)
liveVerification.mode: the rewritten file stays 0600 and no .tmp- file survives the atomic write

suite.before: 371 tests (371 pass / 0 fail) on bf72775 - the card's recorded baseline
suite.after: 383 tests (383 pass / 0 fail, 0 skip) = 371 + 12 new grant-remove tests

whatThisDoesNotProve: no external user has ever run grant-remove
no audit / no author identity in the file
revocation is by scope name only - no partial cap narrowing
two concurrent removals are not ordered beyond the read lease
not a security approval: no audit, no real keys, no outside user
